page.layout: One printed page (left of the scan). Running head at top: left "Lib. III. Cap. X.", right "Vitia & næui magistr.", page number 236 at the top left. Main text in one column: continuation of a paragraph from the previous page, a centred line, a printer's ornament, then the catchword "LIBRI" at the right below the text. The right edge of the scan shows the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed.
page.running_head: Lib. III. Cap. X. / Vitia & næui magistr.

main_text.p: tur opprobriis. Ibidem citatur Gregorius, inquiens: Satis perversum, & contra ecclesiasticam probatur esse censuram, ut frustrà quorundam parentum voluptatibus. suis quis privetur officiis, quem suâ culpâ, vel facinus, ab officii, quo fungitur, gradu non dejecit.
Plura in eandem sententiam eâ-dem distinctione habentur.

page.notes: The printer's ornament (a symmetrical floral vignette) stands between the text and the catchword; it contains no text and is not transcribed. The first line is a continuation: the word "opprobriis" is set in italic together with "tur" and is read as printed. Punctuation in the italic quotation ("voluptatibus.suis", "culpâ, vel facinus,ab officii,quo") is run together in the scan and is copied with the spacing as best seen. The catchword "LIBRI" is set right below the last line. The running head's chapter part is read as "Lib. III. Cap. X." and is included with the title.
